section_summary: This section consists of diplomatic records from the U.S. Embassy in Tokyo dating to August and October 1940, primarily comprising duplicate copies of Embassy Despatch No. 5054 transmitting Report No. 167 ('Report of Conditions in Japan During the Month of August 1940') along with monthly lists of despatches and telegrams sent to the Department of State. The narrative report and communications cover major international developments, including bilateral efforts to resolve the July 7 Shanghai incident involving American marines and Japanese gendarmes, disputes over Shanghai defense sectors following British troop withdrawal, the detention of AP correspondent Relman Morin, and Japanese military demands on French Indochina and the Netherlands East Indies. Internally, the records document the second Konoye Cabinet's proclamation of a 'New National Structure' and 'Greater East Asia' policy, an extensive shakeup and recall of diplomatic personnel under Foreign Minister Matsuoka, expanding state economic controls in the yen-bloc, and intensified pressure against foreign Christian churches and missionary schools in Japan.

subfiles.about: Concluding monthly lists of despatches and telegrams sent by the American Embassy in Tokyo to the Department of State during August 1940, forming an enclosure to Despatch No. 5054.
subfiles.summary: This subfile contains the final portion of the Tokyo Embassy's schedule of despatches (Nos. 4926 through 4941) and the full monthly list of telegrams (Nos. 637 through 771) sent to Washington during August 1940. The entries record diplomatic representations regarding the closure of the Burma route, Japanese demands on French Indochina, defense sectors in Shanghai, anti-British agitation, the detention of journalist Relman Morin, and routine administrative and consular matters. It forms the concluding enclosure section of the first filmed copy of Despatch No. 5054.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 5054: Report of Conditions in Japan During the Month of August 1940 (Enclosures)

subfiles.about: Transmitting the Embassy's monthly report on political, international, and economic conditions in Japan during August 1940, accompanied by complete schedules of despatches and telegrams sent during the month.
subfiles.summary: Despatch No. 5054 transmits Report No. 167, a comprehensive monthly assessment of Japanese foreign policy and internal conditions for August 1940 prepared by the American Embassy in Tokyo with contributions from military and commercial attachés. The report covers U.S.-Japanese friction over the July 7 Shanghai marine incident, contested Shanghai defense sectors, the arrest of AP reporter Relman Morin, and Japanese encroachments upon French Indochina and the Netherlands East Indies. It also analyzes Anglo-Japanese friction following espionage arrests, the announcement of the 'New National Structure' and 'Greater East Asia' policy by the second Konoye Cabinet, a major purge and recall of Japanese foreign diplomats, state economic control regulations, and anti-foreign movements against Christian missions. Appended to the report are complete cumulative schedules of all despatches (Nos. 4876-4941) and telegrams (Nos. 637-771) forwarded by the Embassy to the State Department during August 1940.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 5054: Report of Conditions in Japan During the Month of August 1940

subfiles.about: Duplicate copy of Despatch No. 5054 transmitting Report No. 167 on conditions in Japan during August 1940, covering the table of contents and opening discussions of American-Japanese relations.
subfiles.summary: This subfile comprises the opening portion of a duplicate sextuplicate copy of Despatch No. 5054 from Ambassador Grew, including the transmittal letter, cover page, and detailed index of Report No. 167. It provides the initial pages of the report discussing U.S.-Japanese relations, specifically bilateral diplomatic conversations concerning the July 7 incident in Shanghai involving American marines and plainclothes Japanese military police. The text outlines Ambassador Grew's representations to Foreign Minister Matsuoka urging a restrained local settlement between Colonel Peck and Major General Miura before breaking off at the close of page 478.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 5054: Report of Conditions in Japan During the Month of August 1940
